newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK handover legislature dismisses US boycott snub.
newsitem.headline: HK handover legislature dismisses US boycott snub.

text.p: Hong Kong's controversial handover legislature said on Tuesday it did not care whether U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright stays away from its swearing-in ceremony on July 1.
Amid Western disapproval, the 60-strong provisional legislature, carefully chosen by a China-assembled committee in December, is to replace a democratically-elected assembly.
Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30. Albright is among 4,000 VIPs invited by Britain and China to the historic handover.
"The responsibility of the provisional legislature is to serve the Hong Kong people," a spokesman for its president Rita Fan told Reuters.
"We do not care how foreign powers look at us," he said.

U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Monday Albright would not attend the swearing-in of the China-appointed interim assembly in the early hours of July 1, right after a glitzy ceremony marking the sovereignty change.
It will replace the currently elected Legislative Council as part of China's plan to reverse electoral reforms introduced in the twilight years of British rule.
Britain and its allies, and the pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong, have condemned the body as unnecessary and of doubtful legality.
